b.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)

edges.label: codifies the carve-out
edges.note: The carve-out is in the codified federal regulation, not only in a DoD manual. 32 CFR 117.6(b)(3), 'Responsibilities': "The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07, 'DoD SAP Policy'." The NISPOM Rule was published at 85 FR 83312 on 21 December 2020, so the provision relieving the oversight body has the force of a legislative rule rather than of internal DoD policy. a.label: Carve-Out Provision (DCSA relief from NISP oversight)

b.label: DCSA as DoD Cognizant Security Office under the NISP

edges.label: relieves it of NISP oversight
edges.note: The regulation names the office the carve-out acts on. 32 CFR 117.6(b) makes the Director, DCSA responsible for 'security oversight of the NISP as the DoD CSO', and then (b)(3) removes it: "The Director, DCSA, will be relieved of this oversight function for DoD special access programs (SAPs) when the Secretary of Defense or the Deputy Secretary of Defense approves a carve-out provision in accordance with DoDD 5205.07, 'DoD SAP Policy'." So the effect is not that oversight passes to another body but that the cognizant security office's oversight function ceases for that programme, on the written approval of one of two named officials.
